description: Deterministic normalization tables for the enrichment pilot. Rules are applied top to bottom, first match wins. A raw value that matches nothing normalizes to null and gets a flag; nothing is ever guessed. Patterns are case-insensitive Python regexes.

locked_vocabulary.transmission_variant_other: any other explicit source wording that appears in transmission_named_systems.labels (e.g. 'SelectShift', 'Direct Shift', 'Super ECT', 'ECT-i', 'Tiptronic', 'Steptronic'); never invented
rules: Petrol is canonical. Gasoline / Unleaded / Petrol (Gasoline) normalize to Petrol.
Hybrid and Plug-in Hybrid are separate from Petrol. Hybrid is never silently treated as Petrol.
AWD and 4WD stay distinct. 4x4 / Four-wheel drive / full-time 4WD / part-time 4WD -> 4WD. 4WD is never mapped to AWD.
4x2 / 2WD with no axle stated -> drivetrain null.
Transmission has two levels: family (Automatic|Manual) and variant. A CVT/DCT/AMT belongs to the Automatic family but its variant is never discarded.
Gear counts are kept wherever a source states them.

fuel_type.decision_note: LOCKED: canonical id is 'Petrol'. The app today shows 'Gasoline' in the Sell/Search pickers and the legacy dataset stores 'Petrol (Gasoline)'; both are only label projections of Petrol and are listed below so the comparison is label-independent. Hybrid is NOT Petrol.
fuel_type.legacy_dataset_caveat: The legacy dataset has no Hybrid/Plug-in value: every hybrid is stored as 'Petrol (Gasoline)'. So 'Hybrid' can never appear in CURRENT_CARNET and will always show as MISSING until the product decides how hybrids are represented.

rules.pattern: diesel|\bderv\b|\bd-?4d\b|\btdci\b|軽油|ディーゼル|ดีเซล

explicitly_not_inferred: 'EcoBoost' alone does NOT imply petrol: a source must state petrol/gasoline.
'Turbo' alone does NOT imply a fuel type.

transmission.decision_note: LOCKED two-level representation. transmission_family is Automatic|Manual (what CarNet's pickers offer). transmission_variant keeps the detail: a canonical variant when the source says so (CVT, e-CVT, DCT, AMT, Conventional automatic) otherwise the source's own named system (SelectShift, Direct Shift, Super ECT, ECT-i, ...) otherwise null. 'Conventional automatic' is set ONLY when the source explicitly says torque converter / conventional automatic; a plain 'automatic' or '8AT' keeps variant null (the source did not say). All named systems found are kept in transmission_named_systems. Gear counts are kept wherever stated, including for CVTs (a flag marks them).
transmission.note: An 'automatic' that is also described with 'manual shift mode' / 'sequential shift' is still Automatic (automatic patterns are tested first).

drivetrain.decision_note: LOCKED: AWD and 4WD are DISTINCT canonical values everywhere (evidence, unions, comparison). 4WD is never mapped to AWD. Background: the legacy dataset stores every 4x4 as 'AWD' and the Sell/Search pickers list only FWD/RWD/AWD, so the strict comparison reports 4WD as MISSING_FROM_CARNET. 'legacy_collapse' is used ONLY by the informational legacy_view in the comparison report to show how many MISSING items are pure vocabulary differences; it never touches evidence or unions.

unresolved_rules.note: 4x2 / 2WD does not say whether the driven axle is front or rear. Left null; never assumed RWD.

body_type.basis: sell_step2_fields.dart bodyTypes list. The legacy dataset's 'Off-road vehicle' is already mapped to SUV and 'Pick-up' to Pickup by _mapSpecToFormFields.
body_type.authoring_caution: Toyota calls the 300 Series a 'station wagon (SW)'; that is a Toyota range designation, not a body style claim, so evidence records must leave body_type null for it instead of letting the Wagon rule fire.

seats.note: Accepts an int, a digit string, '7-seater', '7 seats', or a number word. 'up to N' keeps N and sets flag seats_is_maximum. CarNet's Sell picker offers 2,4,5,6,7,8 (sellFlowNearestSeatingLabel rounds others); the union keeps the exact verified count.

rules: 1. Unit cc / cm3 / cm³ / cu cm  -> displacement_cc = value (exact); nominal litres = cc/1000.
2. Unit L / litre / liter with >=3 decimals (e.g. '2.754 L') -> treated as exact: displacement_cc = round(L*1000).
3. Unit L with <=2 decimals (e.g. '2.3L', '3.5-liter') -> nominal only; displacement_cc stays null (never invented).
4. engine_size_label = '<x.x>L' where x = round(cc/1000, 1) when cc is known, else round(nominal L, 1). Half-up on the decimal string.

aspiration.note: Only taken from text the source states. 'EcoBoost' alone is not turned into Turbo.

rules: 1. Strip, collapse internal whitespace to single spaces.

2. trim_key (used for de-duplication and comparison) = casefold, with '-' '_' '/' replaced by a space and whitespace collapsed. So 'GR-Sport', 'GR SPORT' and 'Gr Sport' share one key; 'GXR' and 'GX-R' do NOT (different spelling = different key until a reviewer merges them explicitly).

3. Display value: if the raw string is all upper-case or all lower-case, each space/hyphen/slash-separated part of <=3 letters is upper-cased and longer parts are Title-cased ('PLATINUM' -> 'Platinum', 'xle' -> 'XLE', 'GR SPORT' -> 'GR Sport', 'VX-R' -> 'VX-R'); mixed-case strings are kept as written.
4. The first spelling seen (evidence order) is the display spelling of a key.

market.note: Markets are normalized to CarNet's region_specs codes where one exists, otherwise 'other' + a country slug. A generic 'Middle East' maps to 'gcc' with flag market_approximate. Markets are kept on evidence records for traceability; the model union does not filter by market.
